summary: Univestin is a proprietary standardized botanical blend (free-B-ring flavonoids from Scutellaria baicalensis and flavans/catechins from Acacia catechu; related to the Aflapin/Boswellia line of joint-health ingredients) marketed as a dietary supplement for joint comfort and inflammation. It is positioned to reduce inflammatory mediators (e.g., COX/LOX and 5-LOX pathways). NOTE: Univestin is NOT an FDA-approved drug - it is a dietary supplement ingredient (the FDA does not evaluate supplements for efficacy); evidence derives from manufacturer and small clinical studies rather than a drug label.
indications: Symptomatic relief of joint discomfort and stiffness (e.g., osteoarthritis) - as a dietary supplement
General support of a healthy inflammatory response (supplement claim, not an approved drug indication)

moa: The blend's flavonoid/flavan constituents are reported to modulate inflammatory pathways - inhibiting cyclooxygenase (COX) and lipoxygenase (5-LOX) enzymes and reducing pro-inflammatory mediators (e.g., prostaglandins and leukotrienes) and matrix-degrading enzymes - which is proposed to reduce joint inflammation and discomfort. Mechanistic claims are based on in-vitro and small clinical studies, not regulatory drug review.

missed: If you miss a dose of this supplement, simply take it when you remember or skip it and resume your normal schedule - do not double up. Consistent daily use is generally needed for any benefit.
overdose: No specific toxicity syndrome or antidote is established. Large amounts may cause gastrointestinal upset (nausea, diarrhea). Management is supportive; discontinue the product and seek medical advice if significant symptoms occur.
